messages.author: ab78e227e394cf1d
messages.subject: INLA with spatial varying coefficients
parts:
Hi Authors,

I am trying to build an INLA model with spatially varying coefficients with a continuous covariate.

Should I approach this as below:
```
 inla( Y~  f(spatial_ID, x, model='besag', constr=FALSE, scale.model=TRUE)+
                              f(group)
                            +
                              f(as.numeric(spatial_ID_polar),
                                model = "matern2d",
                                nrow = number_of_gridpoint_x, 
                                ncol = number_of_gridpoint_y 
                              )
                            ,
                            family = "poisson",
                            data = data.frame(x_matrix_2),
                            control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
                            control.compute = list(dic = TRUE))
```
Also if I have multiple spatial covariate will there be any problem if I use any interaction with SVC model?

Alokesh

parts:
Sure! 


I am trying to model a poisson count data (Y) with a few spatial covariates ( for simplicity let us consider only one covariate x). I have tried to model using x as a fixed effect and then separately add a spatial random effect as f(spatial_id, model="iid").

Now I am trying to approach this with spatially varying coefficients, i.e.

y_{spatial_ID} ~ intercept + \beta_{spatial_id,x} x

instead of just:

y_{spatial_ID} ~ intercept + \beta_{spatial_id} x.

How to do that in the INLA model?

Moreover if I have two spatial covariate say x and z, can I add some interaction over them? If it was not spatially varying coefficients I could have just added  as the following:
   
y ~ (x+z)^2

parts:
You can start looking at the Dynamic spacetime regression example at 
https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-stapp.html#sec:dynamic
The hint is to multiply the projector matrix by the covariate values.

There are new ways to implement it: 
 - the (new) 'A.loc' argument in f(...) 
 - the mapper system in the inlabru package

You can also consider the new models implemented in the INLAspacetime package.

best regards,
Elias
